'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)#South Sudan|Spillover of the Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2025 Nasir clashes]]
***The [[South Sudan People's Defence Forces]] capture the town of [[Nasir, South Sudan|Nasir]] in [[Upper Nile State]] from the [[Nuer White Army]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/south-sudans-military-recaptures-key-town-white-army-militia-2025-04-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**The [[Islamic State – West Africa Province|Islamic State]] claims responsibility for a series of deadly attacks targeting [[Christians]] and [[Nigerian Armed Forces|security forces]] in [[Borno State|Borno]] and [[Adamawa State|Adamawa]], [[Nigeria]] earlier this month that killed at least nine people and injured several others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/iswap-claims-responsibility-deadly-attacks-nigeria-2025-04-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[ARK Invest]] becomes the first US-based [[asset management|asset manager]] to gain exposure to the [[Solana (blockchain platform)|Solana]] [[blockchain]] through an [[Exchange-traded fund|ETF]] investment after [[Canada]] approves several [[Spot ETF|spot]] Solana ETFs. [https://coinmarketcap.com/academy/article/ark-invest-funds-become-first-us-etfs-to-add-exposure-to-solana-through-3iqs-staking-etf (Coin Market Cap)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Death and funeral of Pope Francis]]
**[[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|Cardinal]] [[Kevin Farrell]], [[Camerlengo of the Holy Roman Church]], announces that [[Pope Francis]] has died early on [[Easter Monday]], at the age of 88. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/04/21/pope-francis-dies-at-88-the-vatican-says (Euronews)] [https://apnews.com/article/vatican-pope-francis-dead-01ca7d73c3c48d25fd1504ba076e2e2a (AP)]
**Cardinal Farrell, as Camerlengo, becomes the acting head of [[Vatican City]] until the [[2025 papal conclave|next]] [[papal conclave]] in May. [https://www.npr.org/2025/04/21/g-s1-61662/kevin-farrell-camerlengo-vatican-pope (NPR)]
*[[Klaus Schwab]] steps down as leader of the [[World Economic Forum]], which he founded in 1971. [https://www.dw.com/en/world-economic-forum-chairman-klaus-schwab-steps-down/a-72303380 (DW)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2019 El Paso Walmart shooting]]
**The perpetrator of the [[Hate crime|racially motivated]] [[Domestic terrorism|domestic terrorist]] [[mass shooting]] attack that killed 23 people and injured 22 others at a [[Walmart]] building in [[El Paso, Texas|El Paso]], [[Texas]], United States, in 2019, 26-year-old [[2019 El Paso Walmart shooting#Perpetrator|Patrick Wood Crusius]], [[Plea|pleads guilty]] to state charges and is sentenced to [[life imprisonment]] without the possibility of parole to avoid the [[Capital punishment|death penalty]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2025/04/21/el-paso-texas-shooting-walmart-pleads-guilty/83195417007/ (''USA Today'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 Boston Marathon]]
**In [[long-distance running]], [[Kenya]]n road runner [[John Korir (runner, born 1996)|John Korir]] wins the men's competition at the [[Boston Marathon]] with a time of 2:04:45 which, along with his brother [[Wesley Korir]]'s win in [[2012 Boston Marathon|2012]], makes them the first and only set of brothers to win the event. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6296201/2025/04/21/boston-marathon-results-winners-2025/ (''The New York Times'')] 
**Kenyan athlete [[Sharon Lokedi]] wins the women's competition with a time of 2:17:22 and sets the new course record, surpassing [[Buzunesh Deba]]'s record in [[2014 Boston Marathon|2014]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/video/boston-marathon-winners-crowned-history-made-during-2025-race/ (WBZ-TV)]
